title: Year four close
hook: a year with thinkers and schools

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was ahead: the sources read slowly, the poets, a practice of your own. Your line was the summit.

Like water. My attempt. Look as if for the first time. Go to the woods. Solid and light. Thank you. Those lines closed each stretch of this year: the Tao Te Ching, Montaigne, Emerson, Thoreau, the science, and the tour of the world's schools. Read in a row, they sound less like conclusions and more like directions for a walk. Soften. Try. Look. Get outside. Keep what's sure, hold the rest loosely. Say thank you on the way out. Today the year ends, and the first book it opened has one more word for the road.
screen: `LIKE WATER. MY ATTEMPT. LOOK.` → `THE WOODS. SOLID AND LIGHT. THANK YOU.` → `DIRECTIONS FOR A WALK.`

segments.voice: First, four companions, read slowly. Lao Tzu, whose book begins by admitting that words fall short. Montaigne, who wrote about himself in pieces he called attempts. Emerson, who asked readers to look as if for the first time. Thoreau, who went to live by a pond to see what life had to teach. None of them asked to be obeyed. Each walked beside you for a while, then let you go. Second, science, told honestly. Attention, habit and compassion can grow, the studies said, modestly. So the year's rule was simple: keep what's solid, hold the rest lightly. Third, the world's schools, never ranked: Zen halls and Sufi circles, Jewish study pairs and Quaker silence, Hindu chant and Sikh dawn prayer, Chinese parks at sunrise, each met in its own words. This last week asked what drew you, what doesn't fit, and what you actually do. Fourth, water, one more time. The Tao Te Ching, in its eighth chapter, says the highest good is like water. Water benefits everything and doesn't contend. It settles in the low places people look down on. Elsewhere the book adds that nothing is softer than water, yet nothing does better against what is hard. Watch any stream: the water doesn't fight the stone; it goes around. The year's first book gives a fair picture of how to walk out of it: not racing to the top, not standing still, but moving on, steadily and low.
screen: `FOUR COMPANIONS, READ SLOWLY.` · `SCIENCE, TOLD HONESTLY.` · `THE SCHOOLS, NEVER RANKED.` · `WATER, ONE MORE TIME.` · then, large: `ON TOWARD THE TOP.`

segments.voice: If you can stand and move, walk a room or a hallway at half your usual speed, letting your path bend around what's there, a chair, a doorframe, a corner, without pushing anything aside, and letting each step settle before the next. If walking isn't possible, let your breath move like water instead, never forced, or trace a slow, winding path with one hand. Nowhere to arrive; if you pray, you can walk with a prayer.
Year four close. A year with thinkers and schools: four companions read slowly, science told honestly, and the world's ways of practice, each in its own words. Today's word.
Your line: on toward the top. Year five begins tomorrow, reading as a guest. That's year four, complete.

howItsDone: Some people close a year of study with a slow walk, recalling what they read and choosing one line to carry into the next year; some traditions keep a walking meditation of their own.

chat.says: A whole year of thinkers and schools. What's the one thing you're taking from it?

Race to the top now, before I forget everything the year taught me.

chat.meaning: The Tao Te Ching says the highest good is like water: it doesn't contend, and it goes around what's hard. Not racing, not standing still.

Tao Te Ching.meaning: an old Chinese book of short chapters on the Way

Lao Tzu.meaning: the sage tradition names as the Tao Te Ching's author

Montaigne.meaning: a French writer who called his short pieces essays: attempts

Thoreau.meaning: an American writer who lived for a time by Walden Pond

Emerson.meaning: Ralph Waldo Emerson, an American essayist and poet

notes: Tao Te Ching 8 is paraphrased (Legge 1891 not quoted). The line about water going around the stone and the stone changing over time is an everyday picture in the spirit of chapters 8 and 78, not a paraphrase of chapter 8 itself; confirm the framing or cut.
The hook's six lines are the carries of the year's block closes (1144 like water, 1184 my attempt, 1219 look as if for the first time, 1261 go to the woods, 1351 solid and light, 1419 thank you).
'A Frenchman who ... called each piece an attempt' rests on the year's own Montaigne block (carry 'my attempt'); confirm the gloss of essai as 'attempt'.
Original 道 (dao) opens Tao Te Ching 1 (道可道); confirm pronunciation guide 'DOW'.
The practice offers a non-walking alternative for listeners who can't walk.
